output_examples.input: I installed ai-gates. What happens when I first open my project?
output: The plugin session start can copy .ai-gates into the workspace when it is missing.

output_examples.input: How should I begin a new task?
output_examples.output: Enter the PM workflow, then describe the task in plain language. The project PM entry routes the work into the appropriate delivery lane.

output_examples.input: Will a project library upgrade update the Cursor plugin cache?
output_examples.output: No. The project library upgrade changes the project copy. The Cursor plugin cache remains separate and is not updated by that action.

best_practices: Keep job skills in the seeded project tree and treat the plugin skills folder as meta-only.
Use the PM entry point to begin work so the project workflow can select the correct lane.
Upgrade the project library separately from the plugin cache and verify hook ownership after changes.
anti_patterns: Treating the plugin cache as the true skill source after project seeding.
Pulling ai-gates-collect as if it were a skill upgrade.
Duplicating job SKILL.md trees inside the plugin skills folder.

faq.question: What is ai-gates?
faq.answer: It is a Cursor-oriented AI development pipeline with a PM entry and four delivery lanes. This marketplace skill explains how the meta-skill fits into that setup.

faq.question: Where do the planner and developer skills live?
faq.answer: They live in the seeded project, under .cursor/skills and then .ai-gates/skills.

faq.question: How do I start ordinary project work?
faq.answer: Use the PM entry and describe the task. The project workflow then routes the work to the appropriate lane.

faq.question: What happens on the first open of a project?
faq.answer: The plugin session start can copy .ai-gates into the workspace when missing and write runtime metadata that identifies the project owner.

faq.question: Why are two hook sets registered?
faq.answer: The plugin and project may both add hooks. The plugin gate can allow and exit when project hook files exist, leaving the project hooks to do the real work.

faq.question: Does a project library upgrade change the plugin cache?
faq.answer: No. The documented project upgrade uses GitHub tags for the project library and does not update the Cursor plugin cache.
